rfi.description: This week saw France hand out its biggest literary awards, the Prix Goncourt and the Prix Renaudot. But might those numbers rise if reading was a way to meet your soulmate?

rfi.description: The Youth Olympic Games (YOG) are underway in Dakar until 13 November. The first three editions (Singapore 2010, Nanjing 2014 and Buenos Aires 2018) served as a springboard for several champions who made their mark at the Olympic Games between 2012 and 2024. Here are 10 of the biggest names.

rfi.title: Southern African farmers prepare for powerful El Nino with agroecology
rfi.description: Farmer Dudzai Matsapa works under a scorching sun, digging small, shallow pits across his field in Nyanga, east of the Zimbabwean capital, Harare. He will later fill these potholes with organic manure and wait for the rainy season. This is all part of Matsapa’s preparation for the anticipated El Nino, which is expected to trigger drought and extreme heat across southern Africa.

rfi.title: Bread shortage threatens to plunge more Sudanese into hunger
rfi.description: Nearly three and a half years into Sudan's unrelenting war, soaring costs and a nosediving currency have left people like Sawsan Mahmoud struggling to afford even the most basic staple – bread.

rfi.title: Poor facilities held back Senegal's medal-free Youth Olympics team, parents say
rfi.description: As the Youth Olympics continue in Dakar, parents of Senegal's young swimmers are calling for better training facilities and more government support after the country's team finished the competition without a medal.

rfi.title: The art of dressing: how clothes have shaped the image of the artist
rfi.description: How do you spot an artist? Are they the one with the jaunty beret or the dapper silk scarf? Or the tunic covered in paint? An exhibition at the Bourdelle Museum in Paris looks at how wardrobe choices have shaped society’s perception of artists – and made some of them into icons.

rfi.title: Nigeria's plan for state police raises hopes for security and fears of abuse
rfi.description: Nigeria this week took a step closer to a major overhaul of its security system after 28 of its 36 states approved a constitutional reform that would allow individual states to establish their own police forces. Supporters of the move say it will better protect against insecurity on a local level, but concerns have also been raised about the risk of abuse by state governors.

rfi.title: Mbappé returns to France duty as Zidane drafts Pagis into Nations League squad
rfi.description: France head coach Zinedine Zidane welcomed back skipper Kylian Mbappé into his squad for next week's Nations League games against Italy and Turkey and sprang a surprise with the selection of the 23-year-old Paris FC forward Pablo Pagis.

rfi.title: Suez Crisis at 70 reveals the humiliation France tried to keep hidden
rfi.description: Seventy years after France, the United Kingdom and Israel invaded Egypt following its nationalisation of the Suez Canal, the military operation is remembered as a diplomatic disaster. Friday marks the anniversary of a ceasefire that halted the fighting under international pressure, despite the invading forces' success on the battlefield. Archive footage excluded from French cinema newsreels shows the humiliation that followed, as Europe's colonial powers faced the limits of their influence.

rfi.title: Three-quarters of world's displaced people 'on frontlines of climate crisis'

rfi.title: Kenyan cult leader sentenced to 200 years for Shakahola forest deaths
rfi.description: A self-proclaimed preacher from Kenya was sentenced to 200 years in prison on Friday for murdering 191 people, mostly children, by forcing them to starve to death. Hundreds of bodies have been discovered since 2023 at the cult's base near the beach resort of Malindi, in what became known as the Shakahola forest massacre.

Une résurrection pour cette ancienne patineuse de vitesse, victime d'un terrible accident en compétition en 2022. Les médecins lui avaient annoncé qu'elle ne pourrait probablement plus jamais marcher. Après une longue rééducation, Tifany s'est tournée vers le paracyclisme où elle fait désormais partie des meilleures du monde. Prochain objectif : les Jeux Paralympiques de Los Angeles 2028.

france24fr.title: Dialogue nationale en RD Congo : comment sortir de l'impasse ?
france24fr.description: Alors que la guerre se poursuit dans l'Est, cinq grandes figures de l'opposition, réunies au sein de la coalition C64, veulent rencontrer Félix Tshisekedi et Joseph Kabila pour préparer un dialogue national. Mais le pouvoir menace de poursuites ceux qui rencontreraient l'ancien président à Goma. Peut-on encore réunir les acteurs de cette crise autour d'une même table ? Et que devient l'avenir démocratique du pays à l'approche des élections de 2028 ?

france24fr.title: RDC : dialogue impossible entre Tshisekedi, Kabila et l'opposition ?
france24fr.description:
En République démocratique du Congo, la crise politique s'intensifie sur fond de guerre dans l'Est. La coalition d'opposition C64 souhaite rencontrer le président Félix Tshisekedi et son prédécesseur Joseph Kabila pour préparer un dialogue national. Mais Kinshasa menace de poursuites les opposants qui iraient rencontrer l'ancien chef de l'État à Goma, où il dirige désormais un mouvement politico-militaire intégrant l'AFC/M23.

Entre guerre, divisions politiques, débat sur la Constitution et élec

france24fr.title: Patronat et syndicats reçus lundi à Matignon : la colère va-t-elle retomber ?
france24fr.description:
Au menu de Présidentielle 2027: la conférence sociale organisée à Matignon, la démonstration de force de Jean-Luc Mélenchon et la cacophonie de la droite et du centre. 
 
Avec nos invités : Dorian Dreuil, expert associé à l'Observatoire de la vie politique de la Fondation Jean-Jaurès et Anthony Berthelier, journaliste politique au HuffPost.

france24fr.title: CNews : la pétition appelant à la fermeture de la chaîne dépasse le million de signatures
france24fr.description: Lancée pour réclamer la suppression de CNews de l'audiovisuel français, une pétition a dépassé dimanche le million de signatures. Mardi, les députés doivent se prononcer sur la suite à donner à cette initiative : classement sans suite ou examen de la demande.

france24fr.title: Samy Cohen: "Eisenkot est populaire car il représente un apaisement de la vie politique israélienne"
france24fr.description: En Israël, Gadi Eisenkot a été missionné par le président Herzog pour former le prochain gouvernement, dix jours après le résultat des législatives à l'issue desquelles aucune majorité claire ne s'est dégagée. La tâche de l'ancien chef d'Etat-major s'annonce particulièrement complexe. Il affiche sa détermination à réussir et tend même la main au Likoud de Benyamin Netanyahou. Samy Cohen, directeur de recherche émérite au CERI de Sciences Po, était l'Invité d'Au Cœur de l'Info.

france24fr.title: En Israël, Eisenkot invite le Likoud de Netanyahu à participer à une coalition
france24fr.description: Officiellement chargé dimanche de former le prochain gouvernement israélien, l'ex-haut gradé centriste Gadi Eisenkot a appelé à l'unité face à une "crise historique", dont il tient Benjamin Netanyahu pour responsable. Il s'est néanmoins dit ouvert à une coalition avec des élus du Likoud, mais aussi du parti d'extrême droite de Bezalel Smotrich.

france24fr.title: Tennis : Carlos Alcaraz remporte pour la première fois le Masters 1000 de Paris
france24fr.description: L'Espagnol Carlos Alcaraz, 3e joueur mondial, a décroché dimanche son premier titre au Masters 1000 de Paris en battant l'Américain Ben Shelton en finale. Avec ce 29e titre en carrière, il n'est plus qu'à une victoire d'égaler son grand rival Jannik Sinner, qui compte 30 trophées.

france24fr.title: Route du Rhum : "Franchement, c'est un rêve d'enfant", savoure Laperche
france24fr.description: "Franchement, c'est un rêve d'enfant. J'ai toujours vu des images incroyables des arrivées ici, celles des grands champions depuis des décennies. Mon rêve était de courir un jour dans cette catégorie reine des multicoques et de jouer la victoire au scratch" déclare Tom Laperche à son arrivée triomphante.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : Gadi Eisenkot officiellement chargé de former le prochain gouvernement en Israël
Débâcle de Trump aux midterms, revendications lycéennes, JOJ de Dakar : la semaine en images
france24fr.description: Retour sur les temps forts de l'actualité de la semaine écoulée et sur ses images les plus marquantes : la large victoire des démocrates américains aux élections de mi-mandat, la gronde des lycéens qui se poursuit partout en France et les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) de Dakar.

france24fr.title: Yémen : première livraison d'aide médicale du CICR dans la ville de Taëz
france24fr.description: Dr Pierre Catoire, médecin urgentiste vice-président de l'ONG Mehad, est notre invité.

france24fr.title: La Pologne en deuil confrontée au "terrorisme de l'intérieur"
france24fr.description: La Pologne en deuil s'est réveillée choquée dimanche, au lendemain de la tuerie perpétrée à Cracovie par un jeune "fasciné" par les idées d'extrême droite, qui a abattu six personnes et en a blessé quinze.

france24fr.title: Israël : Eisenkot, opposant à Netanyahu, au défi de former une coalition
france24fr.description: Charles Enderlin, journaliste et auteur, est notre invité.

france24fr.title: Inde : bougies, lanternes, et feux d'artifices pour fêter Diwali
france24fr.description: Les célébrations de Diwali ont débuté dimanche. À Ayodhya, considérée comme le lieu de naissance du seigneur Rama – la divinité vénérée lors de cette fête –, les célébrations comprenaient des spectacles inspirés de l’épopée hindoue « Ramayana », des spectacles de lumières et de lasers, des concerts, des feux d’artifice et des démonstrations de drones.

france24fr.title: Au large du Sénégal, au moins 34 personnes sont mortes dans le naufrage d'une pirogue de migrants
france24fr.description: Au moins 34 personnes ont péri dans le naufrage d'une pirogue de migrants au large de Kébémer, dans le nord-ouest du Sénégal, selon les médias publics sénégalais et une ONG. Les recherches se poursuivent pour retrouver d'éventuels survivants.

france24fr.title: Trump veut Dana White, patron de la fédération de MMA, comme porte-parole
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a annoncé samedi avoir proposé le poste de porte-parole de la Maison Blanche à Dana White, un de ses proches qui dirige l'UFC, principale organisation mondiale d'arts martiaux mixtes (MMA).

france24fr.title: "Non au data-center de Rantigny" : manifestation contre le développement de l'IA
france24fr.description: Une manifestation a été organisée pour dire non au futur projet de data center à Rantigny (Oise), ce samedi 7 novembre 2026, réunissant riverains et élus d’opposition.

zeit.title: Krieg gegen die Ukraine: Multinationale Ukrainetruppe beginnt erste Übung in Polen
zeit.description: Unter deutscher Beteiligung will die Ukrainetruppe die Absicherung eines möglichen Friedens im Ukrainekrieg üben. Trump hofft auf Gespräche mit Xi und Putin. Das Liveblog

Weltklimakonferenz COP31: Klimagipfel in der Türkei – Worum es geht und woran es hakt

Leere Kassen: Kommunen sorgen sich um Haushalt 2027
Textilindustrie: Von Socken bis Kampfanzug: Textilbranche baut auf Bundeswehr
Spritpreisdeckel: Hubig kritisiert Pläne von Reiche für Spritpreisdeckel
zeit.description: Justizministerin Stefanie Hubig hält den von Wirtschaftsministerin Katherina Reiche geplanten Deckel für unzureichend. Sie hinterfragt vor allem die vorgesehenen Hürden.

zeit.title: Irankrieg: Marco Rubio verteidigt Krieg nach Kritik aus eigenen Reihen
zeit.description: Der Krieg sei notwendig gewesen, sagt Marco Rubio nach der jüngsten Kritik von Vizepräsident JD Vance. Donald Trump empfängt Katars Ministerpräsidenten. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Kraków: Hunderte Menschen gedenken in Kraków der Opfer des Angriffs
zeit.description: Nach dem Schusswaffenangriff mit sechs Toten haben Menschen in Kraków an einer Gedenkmesse teilgenommen und Blumen abgelegt. Der Tatverdächtige ist in kritischem Zustand.

zeit.title: Papst in Südamerika: Papst ruft vor Milei zu mehr sozialer Verantwortung auf
zeit.description: Papst Leo hat im Beisein von Argentiniens ultraliberalem Präsidenten Javier Milei über Rücksicht auf Schwache gesprochen. Wirtschaft müsse den Menschen dienen, sagte er.

zeit.title: Mauerfall: Ostbeauftragte Kaiser ruft zur Verteidigung demokratischer Werte auf
zeit.description: 37 Jahre nach dem Mauerfall sieht die Ostbeauftragte Elisabeth Kaiser die Demokratie unter Druck. Die SED-Opferbeauftragte fordert einen leichteren Zugang zu Stasiakten.

zeit.title: Bundeshaushalt: Thorsten Frei lehnt Einführung der geplanten Plastiksteuer ab
zeit.description: CDU-Politiker Frei erteilt der Plastiksteuer eine Absage, Matthias Miersch von der SPD verweist auf Gespräche. Im Haushalt könnte ohne die Steuer ein Loch entstehen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Frankreich wird an Ukraine-Gesprächen teilnehmen +++ Russland greift mit Drohnen ukrainische Städte an
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Die USA nach den Midterms: Trump zeigt sich offen für Kompromiss bei Abschiebungen +++ US-Demokraten nehmen Trump und sein Umfeld ins Visier
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus der amerikanischen Innenpolitik im Ticker.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Midterms 2026: Marco Rubio will trotz der Wahlschlappe seiner Partei Aussenminister bleiben
nzz.description: Die Amerikaner haben einen neuen Kongress gewählt. Die Republikaner verlieren ihre Mehrheiten im Senat und im Repräsentantenhaus. Alle Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: USA weiten Blockade gegen Iran auf Landwege aus +++ Israel findet Waffenlager der Hizbullah-Miliz
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Nvidia-Chef Huang hatte mutmasslich eine Affäre mit einer chinesischen Spionin. Das Unternehmen leitet nun eine Untersuchung ein
nzz.description: Jensen Huang räumt eine Affäre ein. Laut Medienberichten vermuten die amerikanischen Behörden, dass die Frau vom chinesischen Geheimdienst angeworben wurde.

nzz.title: Schwere Herzen und ein gebrochener Goalie: Der Fussball verarbeitet die Tragödie um den verstorbenen Jesús de Miguel
nzz.description: «Es kann jeden von uns treffen»: Spaniens Profis wollten am Wochenende nicht spielen, sie mussten aber. Die Trauerfeier für den Stürmer und Familienvater auf Teneriffa war emotional.

nzz.title: Kanzler Friedrich Merz schlägt Ilse Aigner als Bundespräsidentin vor
nzz.description: Dass Ilse Aigner Kandidatin der Union für die Bundespräsidentenwahl werden soll, galt bereits als ausgemachte Sache. Es fehlte aber noch das offizielle Ja des Kanzlers. Jetzt ist es da.

nzz.title: Norris gewinnt Rennen in São Paulo: Mercedes jubelt über die Team-WM
nzz.description: Lando Norris rast in Brasilien zum Sieg. Eine Woche nach Kimi Antonellis WM-Triumph kann Mercedes wieder jubeln.

nzz.title: Rendez-vous für die «cohésion nationale»: Zürcher Schüler sollen Sprachaufenthalte in der Waadt absolvieren
nzz.description: Die beiden Kantone verlängern ihre Partnerschaft für Austauschprojekte von Kindern und Jugendlichen. Bildungsdirektorin Silvia Steiner setzt derweil auf einen Coup im Sprachenstreit.

nzz.title: Der Tabellenführer Lugano verliert in St. Gallen 0:5 – Thun und Basel trennen sich 3:3
nzz.description: Die Resultate der 13. Super-League-Runde im Überblick.

nzz.title: VIDEO - Krakau: Was die Videos vom Angriff zeigen
nzz.description: Ein 24-Jähriger tötet sechs Menschen und fährt anschliessend durch die Altstadt Krakaus. Die Polizei nimmt die Verfolgung auf. Anhand zahlreicher Videoaufnahmen rekonstruieren wir die Route des Angreifers bis zum letzten Schusswechsel.

nzz.title: Busunglück bei Zagreb fordert 2 Tote und 33 Verletzte
nzz.description: Ein Fahrgast berichtet, der Fahrer sei kurz nach einer Pause eingeschlafen. Offizielle Angaben zur Ursache des tödlichen Busunglücks in Kroatien stehen aber noch aus.

nzz.title: Literatur als popkultureller Event: Autoren wie Caroline Wahl, Juli Zeh und Daniel Kehlmann verwandeln sich in Stars
nzz.description: In der Literatur zeigt sich neuerdings eine Entwicklung wie in der Musik: Erfolgreiche Schriftsteller wechseln zu Eventagenturen, Literaturveranstaltungen werden immer teurer.

nzz.title: Schweres Zugunglück in Ägypten: 4 Menschen sterben, 88 weitere werden verletzt
nzz.description: Mehrere Waggons eines Passagierzugs kippen bei einem Unfall seitwärts und landen zum Teil auf Ackerflächen. Das jüngste Unglück in Ägypten reiht sich ein in eine lange Liste schlimmer Unfälle.

nzz.title: Mutmasslicher Besitz von Kinderpornografie: Meghan Markles Vater in den USA festgenommen
nzz.description: Das Verhältnis von Herzogin Meghan zu ihrem Vater ist schon lange zerrüttet. Kürzlich kamen schwere Vorwürfe gegen ihn ans Licht – und führten in den USA nun zu seiner Festnahme.

nzz.title: Die Regierungspartei ANC erleidet ein Debakel bei den Kommunalwahlen in Südafrika
nzz.description: Der African National Congress (ANC) erzielt das schlechteste Ergebnis seit dem Ende der Apartheid 1994. Während die Opposition deutlich zulegt, straften die Wähler die einstige Befreiungsbewegung ab.

spiegel.title: »Tatort«-Vote: Wie gefiel Ihnen »Frei wie ein Adler« mit Ronald Zehrfeld?
spiegel.description: Ein Rocker machte gemeinsame Sache mit einem jungen Mann, der das Downsyndrom hat. Und die Kommissarin musste weinen. Der »Tatort« war diesmal arg tränenselig. Oder sind Sie anderer Meinung?

spiegel.title: Papst Leo in Südamerika: Kritik an Mileis Sparpolitik in Argentinien
spiegel.description: Als erster Papst seit fast 40 Jahren reist Leo XIV. nach Argentinien. Für die Wirtschaftspolitik von Präsident Javier Milei bringt er offenbar wenig Verständnis mit.

spiegel.title: Polen gedenkt der Opfer von Krakau – Schütze noch nicht vernehmungsfähig
spiegel.description: TV-Sender ändern ihr Programm, Konzerte beginnen mit einer Schweigeminute, Hunderte beten gemeinsam: Polen trauert nach den Todesschüssen von Krakau. Gegen den Angreifer wird wegen Terrorismus ermittelt, sein Zustand ist kritisch.

spiegel.title: Kalifornische Küste: Pianist stürzt von Kreuzfahrtschiff und überlebt Stunden im Meer
spiegel.description: Zwei Männer wollten in Südkalifornien Schwertfische angeln. Stattdessen zogen sie einen entkräfteten Musiker aus dem Wasser. Was er ihnen zu seiner misslichen Lage sagen konnte, wirft noch mehr Fragen auf.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: UFC-Chef Dana White als Pressesprecher? »War alles nur Spaß«
spiegel.description: Auf Truth Social hat Donald Trump den Boss der Kampfsportorganisation UFC gebeten, sein Sprecher zu werden. Nach viel Aufregung – und Spott – erklärt der US-Präsident nun: Das war alles gar nicht ernst gemeint.

spiegel.title: Niedersachsen: Ministerin entsetzt über »Gewaltfantasien« von CDU-Chef Sebastian Lechner
spiegel.description: Der niedersächsische CDU-Chef Lechner hat in einer Rede mehr Härte gegen kriminelle Clans gefordert – und martialische Worte gewählt. Ministerin Hamburg von den Grünen sieht darin eine verbale Entgleisung.

spiegel.title: Kim Kardashian: Kunden schimpfen über 148-Dollar-Adventskalender
spiegel.description: Kim Kardashians Modemarke »Skims« hat einen Adventskalender voller billigem Kleinkram verkauft – zu einem stattlichen Preis. In den sozialen Medien hagelt es Häme und Spott. Jetzt reagiert das Unternehmen.

spiegel.title: Nvidia-Chef Jensen Huang entschuldigt sich für Affäre mit mutmaßlicher Spionin
spiegel.description: »Ich war meiner Frau untreu«: Nvidia-Chef Huang hat einen Seitensprung zugegeben, der Konzern leitet eine Untersuchung ein. Seine Geliebte arbeitete offenbar für Chinas Geheimdienst. US-Außenminister Rubio soll vor ihr gewarnt haben.

spiegel.title: Österreich: 61-jähriger Deutscher stirbt bei Wingsuit-Unfall
spiegel.description: Er galt als erfahren, doch nach dem Absprung brach der Kontakt ab: Ein deutscher Wingsuit-Flieger ist in Österreich tödlich verunglückt. Er wurde leblos auf einer Wiese aufgefunden.

spiegel.title: Formel 1: Lando Norris siegt in São Paulo, Mercedes jubelt über Team-WM
spiegel.description: Eine durcheinandergewirbelte Startaufstellung und Regenchaos versprachen Spannung. Immer wieder verloren die Fahrer auf der nassen Fahrbahn die Kontrolle. Doch einholen konnte Lando Norris am Ende niemand.

spiegel.title: Gazastreifen: Zelte versinken im Wasser – Vertriebene ohne Schutz
spiegel.description: Winterstürme bringen erneut schwere Regenfälle in den Gazastreifen. Zehntausende Zelte werden überflutet und sind unbewohnbar. Die humanitäre Lage der rund zwei Millionen Palästinenser verschärft sich zusehends.

spiegel.title: Warum Pilze für das Leben auf der Erde unverzichtbar sind
spiegel.description: Pilze sind für das Leben auf unserer Erde unverzichtbar. Wie sie miteinander »sprechen«, welche Bedeutung sie etwa für die Medizin haben und was für irre Exemplare es gibt, erklärt DEIN SPIEGEL.

spiegel.title: Kirche: Pfarrer Christian Schäfer kellnert im Kasseler Café
spiegel.description: Christian Schäfer ist Pfarrer – und serviert nebenher Kuchen und Getränke in einem Café in Kassel. Mit dem Job verbindet er eine ganz bestimmte Hoffnung.

spiegel.title: Ilse Aigner: Im CDU-Präsidium dürfte Friedrich Merz ihre Nominierung als Bundespräsidentin verkünden
spiegel.description: Ilse Aigner soll Bundespräsidentin werden, die Nominierung trifft in der CDU auf viel Zuspruch. Doch das Verfahren irritiert manchen. Nun werden Details bekannt, inklusive Wanderungen und gemeinsamen Freunden mit dem Kanzler.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump bietet UFC-Chef Dana White Job als Sprecher an - eine Verwechslung?
spiegel.description: In den sozialen Medien behaupten User: Donald Trump sollte gar nicht den Boss der Kampfsportorganisation UFC als Pressesprecher anwerben – sondern eine Frau mit fast gleichem Namen. Die bringt nun Licht ins Dunkel.

spiegel.title: Polen, Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski: Anwohner berichten über den Todesschützen von Krakau
spiegel.description: Wie haben die Menschen in seinem Heimatort den Todesschützen von Krakau erlebt? Und wie reagieren sie nun auf die Tat? SPIEGEL-Reporterin Patricia Friedek war in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski unterwegs.

spiegel.title: Florian Wirtz beim FC Liverpool: Erstes Ligator der Saison gegen Crystal Palace
spiegel.description: Florian Wirtz hatte bislang anderthalb komplizierte Jahre in Liverpool. Nach Tor und Assist gegen Crystal Palace dürfte der deutsche Nationalspieler immerhin mit Selbstvertrauen in die Länderspielpause gehen.

spiegel.title: Brandenburg/Berlin: Leiche der vermissten Lisa gefunden – Verdächtiger festgenommen
spiegel.description: Seit Tagen wurde in Berlin eine Schülerin vermisst. Nun ist in Brandenburg eine Leiche gefunden worden. Die Polizei hat einen schwer verletzten Verdächtigen festgenommen.

observador.title: 2h. PNS garante que casas dadas pela AD são herança do PS
observador.description: O antigo líder socialista acusa o Executivo de Luís Montenegro de se apropriar dos resultados do PS. Ainda, o FCP venceu o Vitória Sport Club por 2-1 e segue invicto no campeonato.

observador.title: 1h. Irão. Secretário de Estado dos EUA rejeita avanços em ne
observador.description: Marco Rubio diz que as exigências do Irão para um acordo de paz são "escandalosas e ridículas". Ainda, a depressão Bruna começa a fazer-se sentir por todo o país durante esta noite.

observador.title: Pedro Nuno defende as acampadas e as assembleias populares
observador.description: Ex-ministro diz que as 32 mil casas entregues pelo Governo da AD devem-se ao trabalho do PS. "A não ser que Montenegro e Pinto Luz andassem a carregar tijolos, não deram um único contributo", diz.

observador.title: A verdadeira luta de Renata Cambra
observador.description: O programa do partido dirigido pelo rosto das acampadas, o Trabalhadores Unidos, é claro: reivindicações como as da habitação não são para tomar à letra, apenas servem para abrir caminho à revolução.

observador.title: As “tendas das periferias” começam a movimentar-se…
observador.description: A Europa vive o seu mais crítico momento desde o termo da Segunda Guerra Mundial e defronta-se, com honrosas exceções, com a pior elite política de que há memória. O que não é pouco.

observador.title: Sobre limites e autoridade
observador.description: É essa autoridade que pais e professores não devem deixar de exercer para que os mais novos possam construir um “eu” saudável e capaz de lidar com as dificuldades da vida

observador.title: A IA vai tirar-me o emprego?
observador.description: Os empregos que ainda não têm nome, a geração que vai ter de os inventar, e o que dizer aos filhos e aos netos.

observador.title: 00h. Ventura vê corrida entre Chega e PS nas legislativas
observador.description: André Ventura afasta PSD da corrida à vitória nas próximas legislativas e deixa críticas aos governos socialistas. No futebol, golo de Pavlidis nos descontos garante a vitória do Benfica na Amadora.

observador.title: Cativações: a austeridade que muda de nome
observador.description: António Costa e Mário Centeno não acabaram com a austeridade. Continuaram a praticá-la sem a chamar pelo nome. Este é o seu verdadeiro legado.

observador.title: A América e o preço da democracia portuguesa (II)
observador.description: Até 1978, Washington convidava os nossos futuros chefes de Governo. Depois, as “jotas” tomaram conta do jardim. E as “jotas” não formam elites: engolem-nas.

observador.title: O euro digital tem de provar que faz falta
observador.description: “Não precisamos de mais um ícone no telemóvel. O euro digital só fará sentido se tornar os pagamentos mais livres, seguros e competitivos.”

observador.title: O PREC voltou. De tenda às costas.
observador.description: Em 2026, por causa das acampadas, importa mais do que nunca, lembrar o 25 de Novembro: nenhuma convicção, por mais intensa, dá a uma minoria o direito de decidir pelos outros.

observador.title: A reforma que ainda não chegou à sala de aula
observador.description: A educação mudou! Ministério reorganizado, devolução do tempo de serviço, apoios a deslocados, currículo em revisão. Falta resolver salário e autoridade do professor, gestão e inclusão pedem cuidado.

observador.title: O equívoco da integração de cuidados
observador.description: Integrar cuidados não é fundir organizações. Integrar cuidados é garantir que o doente deixa de sentir as fronteiras do sistema.

observador.title: Lisboa 360 — Cuidar de tudo o que faz parte da sua vida
observador.description: O crescimento da população, do turismo e do consumo trouxe novas exigências e maior pressão sobre os serviços de higiene urbana. Precisamos de repensar o modelo que resultou da reforma administrativa.

observador.title: Controlar Rendas Não Funciona
observador.description:
Há uma coisa que me incomoda particularmente na discussão sobre a habitação em Portugal.
Questionar as soluções apresentadas para resolver a crise passou a ser quase um ato de insensibilidade social.

observador.title: O mundo que mude de lugar porque uma tenda precisa dele
observador.description: Há uma diferença entre cumprir uma sentença e tentar alargá-la à medida das nossas próprias pretensões.

observador.title: Uma doença rara não cabe numa consulta
observador.description: Três prioridades: encurtar o percurso até ao diagnóstico, garantir cuidados integrados ao longo da vida e conhecer melhor a realidade através de dados atualizados.

letemps.title: En direct, Moyen-Orient – Le dispositif pour bloquer les routes terrestres vers l'Iran «opérationnel», selon Trump

phys-org.description: To date, many of the methods used in clinical simulation have focused primarily on assessing technical skills and compliance with medical standards, often from a generic, interprofessional perspective. phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Tokyo have used a new type of radiocarbon analysis to study a sediment core taken from the Kumano Sea off the coast of Japan. This has revealed multiple "hidden" traces of previously unknown earthquakes in the Nankai Trough, where the country's next megaquake is expected to occur. Reconstructing a more accurate picture of the past will help predict future geophysical events and prepare for potential disasters. The work is published in Radiocarbon.

phys-org.title: Small histone differences help shape gene regulation during sperm development
phys-org.description: Researchers from Kyushu University have found that H3mm15, a histone H3.3 subvariant, contributes to normal sperm development in mice by helping regulate gene expression during spermatogenesis. The findings show that H3mm15 cannot be interchanged with conventional H3.3; although the proteins differ at only three amino acids, they behave differently in chromatin, the DNA-protein structure that packages genetic material.

phys-org.title: How space weather powers auroras in the sky and threatens power grids on the ground
phys-org.description: An aurora is one of nature's most spectacular light shows: It looks like green or red curtains rippling across the night sky. When viewed from the ground, this colorful display might seem far away and disconnected from anything happening on Earth's surface.

phys-org.title: 100 buses long: Scientists map one of the world's largest known coral colonies
phys-org.description: A huge coral colony stretching more than 1.5 kilometers (0.93 miles) along the outer reef of the Cocos (Keeling) Islands has been identified by researchers, making it one of the largest known coral colonies ever recorded.

phys-org.title: New species of ground-dwelling bird, the largest of its kind, identified in same cave as Homo floresiensis
phys-org.description: In 2009, researchers working in the Liang Bua cave on Flores Island came across a leg bone. The 190,000–120,000-year-old fossil was identified as a bird bone and set aside. Like many bird bones before it, it was overlooked and left to collect dust.

phys-org.title: Game theory helps SETI search for alien civilizations
phys-org.description: The search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI) is mostly concerned with where to look for technosignatures from another civilization. Between 2012 and 2015, SETI's Project Phoenix targeted about 1,000 sun-like stars for signs of intelligent life. But where to look might not be as important as when to look, according to scientists at SETI.

phys-org.title: 'Stupendously large' primordial black holes ruled out as a dark matter source
phys-org.description: Primordial black holes are hypothetical objects that could have formed directly from dense clumps of matter in the very early universe. If they exist, their dramatic origins would set them apart from the black holes we see today, which form when massive stars collapse. Some theories suggest that "stupendously large" primordial black holes could account for a significant share of the universe's elusive dark matter.

phys-org.title: Want to fly to the moon? NASA is looking for new astronauts to help grow its Artemis program
phys-org.description: Want to fly to the moon and help build a permanent lunar base? NASA is accepting applications for a new astronaut class that will help grow the Artemis program.

phys-org.title: Chimp sanctuary delivers an ape's food by drone amid Florida floods
phys-org.description: A Florida chimpanzee sanctuary had to deliver food to one of its 200 apes by drone this week because the property was swamped by heavy rain. But the animals stayed safe, and the water finally was receding significantly on Saturday, the organization said.

phys-org.title: Why the tropics lose the most birds when cities expand
phys-org.description: Tropical ecosystems are famous for their teeming, exuberant diversity. In fact, the dramatic increase in biodiversity from the poles to the tropics—known as the latitudinal diversity gradient—is pervasive across branches of the tree of life, and fossil evidence suggests it has existed for millennia.

phys-org.title: Personalized savings reminders can help boost retirement savings
phys-org.description: Private retirement savings are an increasingly important topic in public debate. One popular idea is to phrase savings reminders in one of two ways: either you emphasize what someone stands to lose if they don't save, or you emphasize what they stand to gain if they do. To date, research into which of the two reminder messages is more effective in terms of influencing people's efforts to save has produced conflicting results.

phys-org.title: Student finds proof of rare wild cat in northern New Mexico
phys-org.description: Armed with dozens of motion-sensing cameras, William Grooms spent this past summer documenting wildlife across Carson National Forest in northern New Mexico. It was his first field season collecting photos for a two-year study to understand how forest structure influences biodiversity in the Southern Rocky Mountains.

phys-org.title: The hidden ways insects support animal life—from habitat to health—go way beyond being food
phys-org.description: There are at least 14 million insect species on Earth, and they play highly diverse roles in sustaining the natural world. Insects provide many well-known benefits—what scientists often call "ecosystem services." For example, you can thank a bee or a hoverfly for pollinating wildflowers and agricultural crops, or credit dung beetles for decomposing manure and other waste materials.

phys-org.title: Different text genres help doctoral students adapt their writing to reach new readers
phys-org.description: An academic abstract, a blog post and a public outreach article all place different demands on the writer. Readers' prior knowledge varies, as does the purpose of the text and what needs explaining. Mastering one kind of text therefore does not automatically mean being able to write another.

phys-org.title: Two paths, one flux: Trapped ions simulate Aharonov–Bohm interference in a lattice gauge theory
phys-org.description: In a new Nature Physics study, researchers demonstrated the Aharonov-Bohm effect in a quantum simulation of a lattice gauge theory using a hybrid trapped-ion quantum computer.

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

undark.title: The New Importance of the Scientific Seminar
undark.description: Opinion | The rise of artificial intelligence in science complicates the notion of expertise. When AI can be used to generate ideas, conduct research, and write papers, live scientific presentations — such as public talks and seminars — become more important as a way to demonstrate who is a real expert and who is not.

public-dom.title: “Men with Queer Nerves”: The Jumping Frenchmen of Maine
public-dom.description: In the late nineteenth century, visitors to Maine observed something strange: French-Canadian lumberjacks who, at the slightest stimulus, seemed to jump, strike out with their limbs, or mimic languages they could not speak. Ross Bullen introduces us to these so-called “Jumping Frenchmen” and to their greatest investigator, George M. Beard, who saw a link in their behavior between religious frenzy and neurasthenia.

public-dom.title: Philip Sidney and the Extreme (Dis)graces of the Parenthesis
public-dom.description: Erasmus called them “little moons” and George Puttenham praised them as “figures of tolerable disorder” (if used not too often “nor too thick”). For Philip Sidney, they were simply indispensable. Florence Hazrat introduces us to the uncontested early modern king of brackets and to his romance Arcadia, which abruptly ends, like its author’s life, hanging on a parenthesis.

public-dom.title: “There is Nothing but Immortality!”: Walt Whitman and The Book of Heavenly Death (1905)
public-dom.description: Choice excerpts from *Leaves of Grass* that speak to Whitman’s conception of immortality.

public-dom.title: Anatomy Unzipped: John of Arderne’s Sweden Scroll (ca. 1425–35)
public-dom.description: Early surgical diagrams that present patients prying themselves open for our anatomical gaze.

public-dom.title: In Company Style: Illustrations from James Skinner’s Kitāb-i tashrīḥ al-aqvām (1825)
public-dom.description: An illuminated Persian manuscript about customs, culture, and caste, written by an enigmatic figure of the early British Raj.

public-dom.title: Veronese's Dogs
public-dom.description: “Oh, if I could only pray”, Luther once said of his dog Tölpel, “the way this dog watches the meat”. Attending to attentive canine figures in half a dozen paintings by Paolo Veronese, Thomas W. Laqueur explores the work of an artist whose love of dogs landed him in hot water with the Inquisition.

public-dom.title: It’s “A Cat-astrophe”! (1919)
public-dom.description: “A Cat-astrophe” came on the tail end of an odd 1918 boom in cat-themed music.

public-dom.title: Metamorphosis: Transformations in the Early Modern Flap Book (early 19th century)
public-dom.description: By manipulating paper flaps, the child could turn Adam into Eve into a mermaid, a lion into a griffin into an eagle — all while learning about the inevitability of death.

public-dom.title: The Ties that Bind: Central Asian Ikat (ca. 19th century)

public-dom.title: Artificial Intelligence: Ars Notoria and the Promise of Instant Knowledge
public-dom.description: Centuries before Neo instantly mastered Kung Fu in *The Matrix*, medieval scholars found a shortcut to years of difficult study: a magical manuscript that promised to fast-track advanced learning. Anne Lawrence-Mathers investigates the *Ars notoria*, its supposed powers, and the demonic influence it had upon some users.

proj-syn.title: The Economic Toll of Israel’s Wars
proj-syn.description: Israel’s economy may look strong, but three years of war have inflicted far greater damage than its robust stock market and appreciating currency suggest. Defense spending and government borrowing have risen sharply, while falling output and investment point to a prolonged recession.

proj-syn.title: Rebalancing Nature’s Books
proj-syn.description: The first report card on the implementation of the Kunming-Montreal framework was issued at this year’s UN Biodiversity Conference in Yerevan, and the marks were dismal. The problem is not a lack of targets, but a global financial system that pays to destroy nature and penalizes those who protect it.

proj-syn.title: Only Israel’s Arab Parties Can Restore Its Democracy
proj-syn.description: While Israel’s recent election did not deliver the transformation for which many might have hoped, it could open the way to restoring Israeli democracy. By building a coalition with the Arab-led parties, the opposition bloc could defeat not only Benjamin Netanyahu but also the violent, racist ideology he embodies.

proj-syn.title: Making the Most of America’s Midterm Tsunami
proj-syn.description: American voters’ demand for the rule of law and democracy has helped destroy Trump’s MAGA movement. Affordability may have ranked first among their concerns, but addressing it will depend on repairing and improving democratic institutions.

proj-syn.title: AI Can Help Governments Help Citizens
proj-syn.description: In developing economies, the AI debate has focused less on frontier risk and more on how to ensure that the technology actually serves people. That will require not only designing AI tools to work within government, but also investing in the state capacity required to put the technology to use.

proj-syn.title: MAGA’s Midterm Defeat Won’t Change the Course of History
proj-syn.description: The world must not succumb to euphoria following Donald Trump’s latest defeat. If anything, his lame-duck status deprives Americans and everyone else of an excuse for avoiding hard conversations about the truly radical changes that will be needed to avert future catastrophes.

proj-syn.title: Can AI Colonialism Be Prevented?
proj-syn.description: As the United States and China cement their technological dominance, the AI revolution threatens to reproduce the colonial dynamics of the first Industrial Revolution. To avoid digital colonization, middle powers must work together to build an open AI stack and establish common standards to govern it.

proj-syn.title: Turning Sub-Saharan Africa’s Cities Into Job Engines
proj-syn.description: Cities and towns will be central to creating more and better jobs for Sub-Saharan Africa’s fast-growing population, simply because the region’s people and economic activity are increasingly concentrated there. But unlocking urbanization’s potential requires policy guidance and well-planned investment.

proj-syn.title: Why Are Indian Protesters Targeting the Electoral Commission?
proj-syn.description: Following a “special intensive revision” that struck 130 million voters from the electoral rolls, India’s youth have mounted large-scale protests against the Election Commission. Given the convergence of protests with the formal political opposition, the Commission is unlikely to avoid accountability for mass disenfranchisement.

proj-syn.title: Why Aren’t We Investing More in Climate Adaptation?
proj-syn.description: There are many proven ways to protect people and assets from extreme weather, and such measures often prevent economic losses worth many times their cost. But ensuring their implementation requires making them more affordable and creating innovative revenue mechanisms and financing structures.

proj-syn.title: Put the Ocean at the Center of COP31
proj-syn.description: Last year’s UN Climate Change Conference in Belém, Brazil, put forests high on the climate agenda. This month’s UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Turkey, can do the same for the ocean, whose warming threatens not just food and energy security but global survival.

proj-syn.title: Who's Winning (and Who's Losing) The Ocean?
proj-syn.description: Ahead of COP31, PS sat down with Peter Thomson, the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy for the Ocean, to discuss the logic of “blue” economic development. Watch as he warns of a “world on fire,” takes governments to task for kowtowing to the oil and gas industry, and explains how we can do better for future generations.

proj-syn.title: The Democrats’ Historic Duty
proj-syn.description: While Democrats have good reason to celebrate their historic midterm victory, their current elation must quickly harden into determination. Fortunately, the field for new ideas, systemic and economic, in the US will be the most open it is likely to be for decades.

proj-syn.title: Dot-Com Lessons for the AI Bubble
proj-syn.description: Anyone who lived through the internet boom and bust of the late 1990s and early 2000s should find the current AI investment cycle worryingly familiar. Heavy reliance on debt means that if investors decide to stop lending into the boom, a financial crisis will be inevitable—and far worse than the subprime-mortgage crisis in 2008.

proj-syn.title: China Is Defanging the Dollar, Not Dethroning It
proj-syn.description: China offers Iran and Russia a way to circumvent US sanctions and continue doing business. But this comes at an elevated cost, because these countries are paid in onshore, non-convertible renminbi, which they must then convert into dollars using underground financial networks—tacitly reinforcing the greenback’s dominance.

proj-syn.title: A Fatal Challenge to Mainstream Economics
proj-syn.description: The intellectual project on which mainstream economists were raised, and which still forms the backbone of textbook education, has disappeared. What remains is a pastiche of attempted patches, apologies, and corruptions of “heterodox” ideas, all peddled by exponents of an “orthodoxy” that lacks a theoretical core.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Must Bail Out France
proj-syn.description: If France is to avoid default, the European Central Bank will need to buy large amounts of its government’s bonds through the Transmission Protection Instrument. But meeting this need—and preventing a potentially disastrous eurozone sovereign-debt-crisis—will require the ECB to waive its own rules.

proj-syn.title: The Rise and Fall of Privacy
proj-syn.description: Privacy is not a natural phenomenon, but rather a historical achievement. It emerged after the Reformation and the wars of religion that followed, reached a high point during the Victorian era, and has now been eroding for decades, long before the advent of the digital economy, social media, and AI.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI, Defense And Space Tech Lead For Large Rounds
crunchbase.description: This week brought another plethora of large funding rounds for startups and growth-stage companies. Shield AI, a defense tech player focused on autonomy and virtual simulations, secured the largest financing, bringing in $2 billion. Next on the list was drone delivery provider Zipline International, which pulled in a fresh $1.5 billion.

crunchbase.title: How To Challenge A Monopoly In The AI Age
crunchbase.description: AI chip startups can challenge the sector's Goliath's by building substantially better hardware for emerging inference demands, much as Juniper challenged Cisco with a new architecture suited to the internet’s rapid growth. To win customers, writes guest author R K Anand, co-founder and chief product officer of Tensordyne, challengers must prove their advantages, make switching easy and use small, agile teams to anticipate needs that incumbents have yet to address.
